verifiedFacts.claim: The official Beatles page says "Come Together" was recorded over six days at the end of July 1969, opens Abbey Road, and was connected by John Lennon to a Timothy Leary campaign-song request.

sourceRefs.label: The Beatles
sourceRefs.title: Come Together
sourceRefs.extract: Recorded over six days at the end of July 1969, ‘Come Together’ is the opening track from Abbey Road and according to John, “‘Come Together’ was an expression that Timothy Leary had come up with for his attempt at being president or whatever he wanted to be, and he asked me to write a campaign song. I tried and tried, but I couldn’t come up with one. But I came up with this, ‘Come Together’, which would’ve been no good to him.”

verifiedFacts.claim: The official Beatles page identifies "Something" as George Harrison's Beatles No. 1 ballad, written in 1968, recorded in summer 1969, and included on Abbey Road.

sourceRefs.label: The Beatles
sourceRefs.title: Something
sourceRefs.extract: The one and only Beatles’ No.1 not composed by either John or Paul is George’s beautiful ballad written in 1968, towards the end of the sessions for The Beatles’ ‘White Album’. According to George, “I just got the bit about ‘something in the way she moves’ and then chord progression seemed to follow naturally.” It was finally recorded in the summer of 1969 and included on Abbey Road.

verifiedFacts.claim: The official Beatles page says "Octopus's Garden" was written by Ringo Starr under his real name Richard Starkey for Abbey Road, with George Harrison assisting, and was the last Beatles song released featuring Starr on lead vocals.

sourceRefs.label: The Beatles
sourceRefs.title: Octopus's Garden
sourceRefs.extract: "Octopus's Garden" is a song by the Beatles written by Ringo Starr (under his real name Richard Starkey) from their 1969 album Abbey Road. George Harrison, who assisted Starr with the song, commented: "'Octopus's Garden' is Ringo's song. It's only the second song Ringo has ever written, mind you, and it's lovely." He added that the song gets very deep into your consciousness "...because it's so peaceful. I suppose Ringo is writing cosmic songs these days without even realising it." It was the last song released by the Beatles featuring Starr on lead vocals.

sourceRefs.extract: "Golden Slumbers" is a song by the Beatles, part of the climactic medley on their 1969 album Abbey Road. verifiedFacts.claim: The official Beatles page says "Her Majesty" was written by Paul McCartney, credited to Lennon-McCartney, is Abbey Road's final track, appears fourteen seconds after "The End", and was not listed on the original sleeve.

sourceRefs.label: The Beatles
sourceRefs.title: Her Majesty
sourceRefs.extract: "Her Majesty" is a song written by Paul McCartney (although credited to Lennon-McCartney) that appears on the Beatles' album Abbey Road. It is a brief tongue-in-cheek music hall song. "Her Majesty" is the final track of the album and appears fourteen seconds after the song "The End", but was not listed on the original sleeve. As such, it is considered one of the first examples of a hidden track in rock music.
